label: TSMM to AIS-1 experimental binding
description: Maps AIS-1 bonded agent identity concepts into TSMM abstractions so AIS-1 can be compared with other trust systems without treating bonded identity as a complete delegation or assurance stack. This binding is experimental and should be read as a comparative modeling surface, not as a maturity or endorsement signal.

mappings.description: Public bonded-agent identity surface describing the software agent that participates in downstream interactions.
Accountable sponsoring party that stands behind the agent and supplies the governance anchor for the bond.
Persistent accountability linkage interpreted as a governed trust state that an agent is sponsor-backed under stated terms.
conditions: The bond does not by itself prove action-level delegation or authority to perform consequential operations.

mappings.description: Durable agent identifier that roots the bonded identity surface and can be referenced across verifiers, registries, and policy decisions.
Tiered claim about the strength of the published agent identity and sponsor backing, interpreted as a profile-governed trust input rather than as an unconditional authority grant.
Verifier-side evaluation outcome produced from bond lookup, status checks, and policy interpretation.
Lifecycle-affecting state transition that should downgrade or terminate reliance on the bonded identity surface.

notes: AIS-1 fits TSMM best as a bonded agent identity and accountability surface.
AIS-1 bond state is modeled as trust-relevant status, not as a substitute for delegation semantics, runtime authorization, or full provenance guarantees.
This experimental binding keeps AIS-1 inside the comparison surface while making its current maturity boundary explicit.
The binding is intended to support cross-repo normalization across TSMM, trust-infrastructure-schemas, and ANAB.

guarantees.name: bonded-identity-modeling
guarantees.description: AIS-1 agent, sponsor, tier, and bond constructs can be represented through TSMM agent, governance, profile, assessment, and effect abstractions.

guarantees.name: lifecycle-visibility
guarantees.description: Bond verification, suspension, and revocation events can be represented as trust-relevant lifecycle changes in TSMM.

guarantees.name: delegation-completeness
guarantees.description: AIS-1 can contribute identity and accountability context, but action-scoped delegation and runtime authorization remain outside the current substrate.

limitations.name: no-native-delegation-object
limitations.impact: TSMM can describe what AIS-1 does not yet formalize: mandate objects, invocation constraints, and delegated authority chains.
limitations.mitigation: Pair AIS-1 identifiers with a delegation profile or external authorization surface when consequential actions are involved.

limitations.name: provenance-scope-gap
limitations.impact: Bond verification does not by itself provide message-level authenticity or end-to-end provenance.
limitations.mitigation: Compose AIS-1 with protocol-level integrity and evidence-bearing artifacts where transport or content trust matters.

limitations.name: experimental-maturity-boundary
limitations.impact: TSMM models AIS-1 for comparison without treating the current binding as a mature or complete trust-stack profile.
limitations.mitigation: Use the maturity taxonomy in docs/maturity-model.md and pair AIS-1 with separate delegation, policy, and provenance mechanisms for consequential use.

behavioralExpectations.expectation: Verifiers treat AIS-1 tier and bond state as identity-and-accountability signals, not as blanket authority to act.
Downstream repos preserve issuer, sponsor, bond-status, and evidence references so AIS-1 artifacts can be reused without local semantic drift.

notes: AIS-1 is included for comparative modelling and architectural evaluation.
This binding does not imply broad interoperability maturity or production endorsement.
Delegation, runtime authorization, and provenance remain out of scope for this binding.
